newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fortunes vary as French politicians pen columns.
newsitem.headline: Fortunes vary as French politicians pen columns.

text.p: French politicians, from President Jacques Chirac down, are turning columnists with varying fortunes as the campaign for the May 25-June 1 election steps up pace.
Chirac was the first to pen an article urging voters to back his ruling conservatives in the two-stage parliamentary poll.

The 64-year-old Gaullist offered his column to 14 major provincial newspapers, faxing his text to the chosen press on Tuesday of this week. But national dailies managed to get it and also published it on Wednesday. Those who were not offered it were furious.

Avoiding that slip, opposition Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin offered a column to all French newspapers. Most published it on Friday -- with the notable exception of his Communist allies' daily, L'Humanite.
Far-rightist Jean-Marie Le Pen sent his own column to all regional dailies on Wednesday -- and all appeared to have boycotted it, a spokeswoman for his National Front party said.
The next column is expected from Communist Party leader Robert Hue later this week.
